 India need 226 runs to win in 20 overs to beat New Zealand in the first T20I match at Hagley Oval in Christchurch
 India vs New Zealand India 1st T20I live streaming details
 Our Bureau New Delhi 6 min read Last Updated : Oct 22 2026 | 2:39 PM IST New Zealand posted a challenging total of 225 for 5 against India in the first T20I at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Thursday, with Glenn Phillips leading the hosts' batting charge with an unbeaten 82 off 40 balls. The hosts recovered from the loss of three wickets to build a formidable total, setting India a target of 226 runs to win the match and take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.   Finn Allen and Tim Seifert provide brisk start   After India won the toss and opted to field, New Zealand openers Finn Allen and Tim Seifert began cautiously before shifting gears to put pressure on the Indian bowlers. The pair added 49 runs for the opening wicket before Mayank Yadav dismissed Seifert for 24 off 17 balls.     Allen continued the aggressive approach, scoring 45 off 24 deliveries, before Axar Patel removed him to give India their second breakthrough.   Daryl Mitchell survives dropped catch before dismissal Also Read

   India had an opportunity to strengthen their position in the 11th over when Abhishek Sharma dropped a catch offered by Daryl Mitchell off Mayank Yadav's bowling. Mitchell was batting on 16 at the time and made the most of the reprieve, adding another 12 runs before Arshdeep Singh dismissed him for 28 off 19 balls.   Glenn Phillips and Bevon Jacobs turn the momentum   Phillips and Bevon Jacobs shifted the momentum with an aggressive partnership for the fourth wicket. The pair added 73 runs, helping New Zealand accelerate towards a big total.   Phillips reached his 13th T20I half-century in just 23 balls, continuing to find boundaries as India struggled to contain the scoring rate. Jacobs contributed 31 off 16 deliveries before his innings ended at the non-striker's end when Arshdeep Singh effected a run-out with an athletic effort in his follow-through.   Phillips powers New Zealand to imposing total   Phillips remained unbeaten on 82 off 40 balls, providing the finishing impetus alongside Michael Bracewell, who made seven not out off six deliveries. Their efforts took New Zealand to 225 for 5 in 20 overs, giving the hosts a strong platform to defend.   The total was New Zealand's highest in men's T20 internationals at home, leaving India needing 226 runs for victory in the series opener.   New Zealand scorecard:   New Zealand (20 ovs maximum)

   The coin flip of the match went in India's way who opted to field first.   Captains' take after toss:   Mitchell Santner (NZ):  We were going to bowl. Looks a fresh wicket. Guys are really excited for a big series. It's cool to play against India. The depth we've got is really good. (On Bevon Jacobs) He's shown what he can do, lot of power in the middle-order.   Shreyas Iyer (IND):  We'll bowl first. Quick turnaround, got to see how the wicket will play. Pretty well, a lot of them took time to get used to the conditions. Everyone is professional. A lot of positives, especially in the batting. Bowling-wise, it wasn't easy to bowl. Reddy and Mayank come in.   New Zealand vs India 1st T20I playing 11:   New Zealand playing 11:  Finn Allen, Tim Seifert (wk), Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Bevon Jacobs, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (c), Nathan Smith, Matt Henry, Adam Milne, Lockie Ferguson   India playing 11:  Sanju Samson(w), Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan, Shreyas Iyer(c), Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Naman Dhir, Axar Patel, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Arshdeep Singh, Mayank Yadav     Check all the live updates of the New Zealand vs India 1st T20I match from Christchurch here   Now, keeping all this in mind, let’s take a look at how fans from across the globe can watch the match live.   New Zealand vs India 1st T20I broadcasting details
